§1
Warm-Up · Quick Fire
Activate can / like / need · Real work context · Collect errors for §5
5–8 min
Real Skills
What Do You Like?
What Do You Need?
At Work Today
T–S · Question 1
Ask your partner: "Can you speak English?" — Full sentence back: "Yes, I can — a little!" or "I can speak a little, but I can't speak fast yet."
S–S · Question 2
Name 3 things you like at work. Use "I like [noun]." — Nouns only. "I like coffee" ✅ · "I like drinking coffee" ❌ (that's A2.1 territory!)
Class · Question 3
Look at your desk right now. Name 3 things you need. "I need a ___ / I need ___." Go around the room — no repeating objects.
Teacher Note
Collect 3–4 student sentences on the board — mix of correct and incorrect. Watch for: "I like drinking" (gerund ❌) · "I can to speak" (infinitive after modal ❌) · "She need" (missing 3rd person -s ❌). Do NOT correct yet — create curiosity. Use these for §5.
⚡ Quick Win — 20 seconds
Say out loud: "I can speak English. I like coffee. I need a pen." — Three structures. One breath. You already know this.
5 min · 3 questions · Badge ⚡ when done
§2
Speaking · Skills, Likes & Needs at Work
3 rounds · T–S / S–S / Class · Model answers with reveal
8–10 min
T–S
Your manager at Vertex Logistics, Celaya asks: "What can you do in this role?"
Give 3 real skills using CAN + base verb. No "to". Be honest about limits.

"I can use Excel and I can write reports in Spanish. I can't design graphics yet — but I can learn fast!"

can + BASE verb · no "to" · "yet" = honest + professional

S–S
"What do you like about your job? And what do you NOT like?"
2 things you LIKE + 1 you don't. Nouns only. Use: "I like [noun]. I'm not really into [noun]."

"I like the teamwork and the variety. I'm not really into long meetings."

"I like the teamwork" ✅ · "I like working with the team" ❌ (gerund = A2.1)

Class
"What does your team NEED to work better this month?"
One NEED sentence per person. Go around. Note 3rd person: she/he needs (with S!).

"We need a faster internet connection. My manager needs a new laptop. I need a charger."

She/He NEEDS (with S) · I/We/They NEED (no S) — never forget this

Teacher Note — Engagement Layer
After Round 3, ask: "Who has the most interesting NEED?" Vote with hands. The winner reads their sentence again — louder, slower, with confidence. Creates memorable production moment.

Teacher Note — can/can't Minimal Pair
"can" /kæn/ (short, unstressed, schwa vowel) vs "can't" /kɑːnt/ (stressed, clear A, T at the end). Drill 5×: thumbs up = can, thumbs down = can't. "She can drive" — "She can't drive". Make the difference audible before activities.
🗣️ Micro-Speaking — 45 seconds
Choose 3 words. Make one sentence with each using can, like, or need. Say them out loud to your partner.
Model: "I can fix computers. I like tea. I need a folder."

§4
Colloquial · 4 Phrases for This Week
Cafetería · requests · preferences · Context and drill
5 min
"Sure, no problem!"
Responding to "Can you...?" — natural, professional. Replaces the stiff "Yes, I can."
A: "Can you send the report?" B: "Sure, no problem!"
"I'm not really into [X]."
Polite way to say you don't like something. Always + NOUN. Never + gerund at A1.1.
"I'm not really into soda — can I get a water instead?"
"Can I get a…?"
American English informal ordering. Very common in maquiladoras and multinationals in the Bajío.
"Can I get a black coffee and a sandwich, please?"
"Anything else?" / "That's all, thanks."
"Anything else?" = ¿Algo más? "That's all, thanks." = Eso es todo, gracias.
"Anything else?" — "That's all, thanks."
Teacher Note — Cafetería Drill (2 min)
Teacher plays server. Student: "Can I get a coffee." Teacher: "Anything else?" Student: "That's all, thanks." Three quick rounds. Then swap: student is the server. The drill trains the full exchange.
§5
Grammar · Can / Like / Need — Discovery
Problem → Tool format · Elicit from board · Activities + Quick Poll · Badge ⚡
10–12 min
🚨 Real Situation
Your US manager emails: "Tell me — what can you do, what do you like about this job, and what do you need?"
You want to say: "Puedo usar Excel, me gusta el equipo, y necesito una laptop nueva."
❓ How do you say this correctly in English?
✅ Three Tools
"I can use Excel" → CAN + base verb (NEVER "can to use")
"I like the team" → LIKE + noun (NEVER gerund at A1.1)
"I need a new laptop" → NEED + a/an + noun
Structure✅ Affirmative❌ Negative❓ Question
can / can't I can speak English.can + BASE verb · no "to" I can't fix it.can't + BASE verb Can you drive?Can + subject + BASE?
like + noun I like coffee.like + NOUN · no gerund at A1.1 He doesn't like rice.don't/doesn't + like + noun Do you like salad?Do/Does + subject + like + noun?
need/want + noun I need a charger.need + a/an + noun I don't want water.don't/doesn't + want + noun Does she need paper?Do/Does + subject + need + noun?
⚠️ Top 3 errors — zero tolerance, correct immediately:
✘ "I can to speak" → ✅ I can speak — base verb after can, never "to"
✘ "I like drinking coffee" → ✅ I like coffee — noun only at A1.1, no gerunds
✘ "She need a pen" → ✅ She needs a pen — 3rd person -s, always, no exceptions
⚡ Quick Poll — 3 Grammar Questions
Loading...
✏️ Activity A — Choose the Correct Form
1. My colleague ___ use SAP — she learned it last year.
2. I ___ long meetings — they slow everything down.
3. The director ___ a new report by Friday.
4. ___ you speak English? — Yes, a little!
🗣️ Micro-Speaking — 60 seconds
Tell your partner one real sentence using each structure: "I can ___ / I like ___ / I need ___." Use vocabulary from §3. Partner checks: no "to" after can, no gerund after like.
✏️ Activity B — True or False?
"I like working here" — correct at A1.1 (gerund after LIKE is OK).
"Can you help me?" — correct and natural way to ask for help.
"She don't like rice" — correct negative for 3rd person.
"I need pen" (without article) — correct English for singular countable noun.
§6
Listening · Sofia's First Week at Vertex
Monologue · Skills · Likes · Needs · 4 comprehension questions · Badge 🎧
8–10 min
Sofia's First Week — Vertex Logistics, Celaya
A1.1 · M5 · S3A · Voice: Juliet (ElevenLabs) · 128 kbps
0:00 0:00

Hi! My name is Sofia Reyes, and I'm a new coordinator at Vertex Logistics here in Celaya. Today is the end of my first week, and I want to tell you about my job.

So, what can I do? I can speak English and Spanish — that's why they hired me! I can also use Excel and Word, and I can write reports. I can't drive a company vehicle yet, but I'm learning. And I can't manage a team — I'm still new. But I can learn fast, and I want to.

What do I like about this job? I like the team — everyone is very friendly. I like the office too — it's modern and quiet. And I really like the cafetería. The coffee is great! I'm not really into the long Friday meetings, but I understand they're important.

What do I need? Right now, I need a new charger — mine is broken. I also need a folder for my documents, and I need a pen! I left mine at home today. My manager needs some information from me by Monday, and the team needs a better printer — the one we have is very slow.

So — can I do this job? Yes, I can! I like it here, and I need to learn a lot. But that's okay. See you next week!

📎 ElevenLabs: Voice — Sofia (American English) · Speed 0.78 · Pitch 1.0 · A1.1 M5 S3A · ~170 words

Teacher Note — Pre-listening task
Before playing: write on board — "What CAN Sofia do? What does she LIKE? What does she NEED?" Students listen once for gist, then a second time for answers. Do NOT show script until comprehension questions are complete.
1. What can Sofia do? Choose TWO correct answers.
2. What does Sofia like about her job?
3. True or False: Sofia needs a new charger because hers is broken.
4. True or False: Sofia can already manage a team at Vertex.

Speaking Cards — Can / Like / Need
6 prompts · 30 seconds each · speak first, think second
Card 1 / 6
CARD 1 OF 6
Name 3 things you CAN do at work that your colleague can't.
Use: "I can ___ but [name] can't ___."
CARD 2 OF 6
What do you NEED right now — at your desk, in your life, at work?
Use: "I need a ___ / I need ___." (3 things, different categories)
CARD 3 OF 6
Describe your ideal lunch. What do you like? What are you not really into?
Use: "I like ___ / I'm not really into ___ for lunch."
CARD 4 OF 6
Your manager asks: "Can you finish the report today?" — What's your honest answer?
Use: "Yes, I can ___." OR "I can't ___ today because ___."
CARD 5 OF 6
What does a perfect workplace NEED? Name 3 things the team or office needs.
Use: "A good workplace needs ___ / The team needs ___."
CARD 6 OF 6 ⭐
You are Sofia at Vertex. Introduce yourself using CAN, LIKE, and NEED in 5 sentences.
Model: "I can ___ / I like ___ / I need ___ / I can't ___ yet / I'm not really into ___."
1 / 6
30 sec per card · speak first · timer starts the pressure

✅ I Can Now… — Click each one when confident
I can use CAN + base verb correctly — and CAN'T for honest limits. No "to" after can. Ever.
I can use LIKE + noun — NOT a gerund. "I like coffee" ✅ / "I like drinking coffee" ❌ at A1.1.
I can use NEED + article + noun to express what I need at work. 3rd person: SHE NEEDS.
I can order at a cafetería using "Can I get…?" and respond with "That's all, thanks."
I can introduce myself using all 3 structures in 60 seconds — no notes, no hesitation.
"Sure, no problem!"
Use every time someone asks "Can you…?" this week. One phrase replaces your old silence.
"Can I get a ___?"
Order in English at the cafetería tomorrow. Even one sentence = real progress you can feel.
"I can ___, but I can't ___ yet."
Use when someone asks about your skills. "Yet" signals you're growing — professional and honest.
